chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, who said:
I asked him about a man who designates his owned slave for posthumous emancipation. Does he have the right to go back on it? He said: "Yes, it is like a bequest."

key_terms.يَرْجِعَ: to retract or revoke the decision
key_terms.يُدَبِّرُ: to designate a slave for emancipation after the owner's death

ai.seo_question: Can a person revoke the declaration of emancipation of a slave after death in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning tadbīr, the declaration that a slave will be freed after the master's death. The Imam عليه السلام states that such a declaration has the status of a bequest, meaning it may be revoked during the person's lifetime.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5565 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who designates his slave for emancipation after his death (mudabbar). Can he revoke this decision?
Imam (as) said: "Yes, it is like a will."
